basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 11.' and it opens '(Vers. 11.) De terra illa exiit Assur, et aedificavit Ninivem, et Robooth civitatem. De'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 11.) De terra illa exiit Assur, et aedificavit Ninivem, et Robooth civitatem. De terra hac Assyriorum pullulavit imperium, qui ex nomine Nini Beli filii, Ninum condiderunt, urbem magnam, quam Hebraei appellant NINIVEM. Ad cujus vel ruinam vel poenitentiam, tota Jonae pertinet prophetia. Quod autem ait: Ninivem et Rooboth civitatem, non putemus duas esse urbes: sed quia Rooboth plateae interpretantur, ita legendum est: Et aedificavit Niniven, et plateas civitatis.
